physical_mismatches.reason: No block floorplan is published. There are no x, y, width or height values for the cores, L2 caches or other blocks, and Figure 6 is an architecture diagram, not geometry. A steady 2D Studio floorplan therefore cannot be built from the paper without inventing geometry.

Table 1 gives per-task (benchmark) leakage and dynamic power, not per-block power for the same scenario. The paper does not publish a rule for mapping tasks to per-core block power, and the task-to-core assignment per hyper-period is only shown in figures. Total chip power cannot be split into per-block power without inventing a rule.

The original study is transient and scheduling-driven. It uses 10 hyper-periods of about 14 s with core temperatures feeding back into task assignment. A steady 2D thermal solve cannot reproduce the transient peaks or the assignment feedback loop.

The optimizer (GA task assignment) and controller (per-period thermal-aware scheduling under EDF) act on workload allocation, not on a floorplan or package parameters, so they have no counterpart in a static Studio steady-state solve.

The HotSpot package, cooling and material parameters (R and C values, heat sink, TIM, die thickness, ambient coupling beyond the 45 C ambient) are not reported, so the original thermal solver setup is not reproducible.

The system is a planar quad-core CPU with no 3D stacking, interposer or advanced cooling. These are not mismatches with a 2D Studio package, but they confirm that the paper's contribution is scheduling and not geometry.
